answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can require each account to lock a refundable bond before bidding, then slash it when independent audits expose duplicate identities or fabricated work. A haven for verified agents emerges only when the attacker must fund every identity; even at low bond size, thousands of copies tie up capital and risk forfeiture, while a nebula of disposable accounts gains no payout without costly, distinct proofs. A cipher-backed audit log makes reuse detectable.
